props.title: Revenge of the Pink Panther
props.initialSlug: Bumbling Inspector Clouseau fakes death to catch mob

sections.content: Revenge of the Pink Panther (1978) marks Peter Sellers' final completed performance as the bumbling Inspector Clouseau, delivering peak slapstick chaos in the celebrated Pink Panther series. Sellers' physical comedy reaches masterful heights, particularly in the Hong Kong disguise sequence and the psychiatric hospital escape. The film follows the successful formula established in The Pink Panther (1963) and perfected in The Pink Panther Strikes Again (1976), blending elaborate pratfalls with Clouseau's mangled French accent. Director Blake Edwards, in his sixth Panther collaboration with Sellers, maintains the series' signature mix of broad comedy and surprisingly complex action setpieces.

sections.content: The film's success relies heavily on the established chemistry between Sellers and Herbert Lom as the increasingly unhinged Chief Inspector Dreyfus. Their dynamic, perfected over five previous films, reaches its comedic zenith here. The Hong Kong setting expands the series' scope while maintaining its European charm, similar to how Casino Royale (1967) - another Sellers vehicle - attempted to globalize its comedy. The film's elaborate action sequences, particularly the dockyard chase, demonstrate Edwards' growing confidence in mixing comedy with genuine thrills.

While Revenge of the Pink Panther represents the end of Sellers' living portrayal of Clouseau, it influenced countless comedy franchises that followed. Its DNA can be seen in Naked Gun: From the Files of Police Squad! (1988), Austin Powers: International Man of Mystery (1997), and even modern action-comedies like Johnny English (2003). The film's balance of physical comedy and international intrigue created a template that comedy filmmakers continue to reference. SUBHEAD: Legacy and Influence

The Pink Panther series' impact on comedy filmmaking cannot be overstated. Henry Mancini's iconic theme music and the animated pink panther in the credits sequence became cultural touchstones. Later attempts to revive the series, including Trail of the Pink Panther (1982) using unused Sellers footage and Steve Martin's reboot The Pink Panther (2006), demonstrate the enduring appeal of the character while highlighting Sellers' irreplaceable contribution.
